title: Longest Common Subsequence
source: canonical Longest Common Subsequence concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The inputs are two lowercase strings. Return the length of their longest common subsequence: the longest run of characters that appears in both strings in the same relative order, without needing to be adjacent in either.
constraints: both strings consist of lowercase letters

examples.explanation: "raity" appears in both strings in order: r, a, i, t, y.
"suday" appears in both strings in order.

hints: Compare the strings from their ends: matching last characters extend a common subsequence by one.
When the last characters differ, the answer is the better of dropping one character from either string.
A table over prefixes of both strings fills in O(m * n); matching characters take the diagonal plus one, mismatches take the better neighbor.
solution: Table over all prefix pairs: equal characters extend the diagonal value by one, unequal characters inherit the better of the two neighbor prefixes. O(m * n) time, one rolling row of O(min(m, n)) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include identical strings, no shared characters, and interleaved matches

visible.failNote: subsequence characters keep their relative order
shared characters need not be adjacent
